what_its_for: Nisoldipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It belongs to a group of medicines called calcium channel blockers, which work by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, split, or break the tablet. Take it on an empty stomach or with a light, low-fat meal. Do NOT take it with a high-fat meal, grapefruit, or grapefruit juice, as these can cause too much of the medicine to enter your bloodstream. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how your blood pressure responds. A common starting dose is 17 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose every 7 days up to a maximum of 34 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember the same day. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store nisoldipine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can raise the level of nisoldipine in your blood to dangerous levels. Avoid high-fat meals right before or after taking your dose. Limit alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and cause dizziness. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine may cause dizziness. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain or tightness, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, shortness of breath, severe headache, or skin rash. Also call your doctor if your blood pressure readings remain high or if you feel worse after starting this medicine.
when_it_works: Nisoldipine starts lowering your blood pressure within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit. Even if you feel well, keep taking this medicine every day. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so it is important not to stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65) and people with liver problems may need a lower starting dose because the medicine stays in the body longer. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as nisoldipine may not be safe during pregnancy. This medicine is not approved for use in children. Always give your doctor a full list of all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with nisoldipine.
